frontier.hypothesis: Target's blocked-but-unallocated $a1 and $a2 come from global.c's pass-0 regs_someone_prefers exclusion, not from anything being live in those registers.
frontier.mechanism: prune_preferences builds regs_someone_prefers[A] from the full preferences of every lower-priority CONFLICTING allocno (minus A's own when sizes are equal) and find_reg ORs it into `used` on pass 0. A register that another allocno merely PREFERS is therefore unavailable even though no value occupies it — the only known mechanism that reproduces target's signature of 39 instructions that never mention $a1 or $a2 while its allocnos climbed past both.
frontier.next_probe: Reconstruct, per allocno, hard_reg_full_preferences / regs_someone_prefers / the allocno_order priority for the candidate and v_f basins (the .greg dump prints raw preferences and conflicts but not the pruned sets). Then search for a C shape where a LOWER-PRIORITY allocno carries a full preference on 5 and 6 — a copy to or from those hard registers that survives flow — without being live in them where the a1/pointer allocnos are allocated. Priority is allocno_order (live-length + reference count), which statement order changes directly.

frontier.hypothesis: The v_f basin is not a dead end despite scoring 14-19: it is the only basin where the missing 39th instruction exists at all, and it is now exactly one blocked register away from target's allocation.
frontier.mechanism: In v_f the a1 allocno sits at 6 (target 7) and the pe62 allocno at 7 (target 8). Every exclusion mechanism measured so far also OCCUPIES the register, and the occupancy disorders the schedule (cam_val lands in $a1, its D_80101E6C store slides to the end of the function).
frontier.next_probe: Re-sweep the v_f basin optimising the STORE SCHEDULE alone, keeping the third parameter as a diagnostic scaffold: if an order exists in which the D_80101E6C store stays adjacent to its load WHILE the a1 value stays live to the end, the basin drops below 13 and the remaining work is swapping the scaffold for a preference-only mechanism (frontier item 1).

frontier.hypothesis: candidate.c's two /* FAKE */ pointer aliases have now gone FIVE sessions (s3-s7) without a layer-2 cheat-reviewer verdict.
frontier.mechanism: pointer-alias-fake-exception is a sanctioned last-resort family requiring documented lever-exhaustion + a named GCC-pass mechanism + a /* FAKE */ annotation; candidate.c supplies all three and the exhaustion record grew again this session. A FAIL reverts the floor 13 -> 17 and invalidates both frontier entries above.
